info.name: OpenAI Playground — Responses vs Chat Completions
info.description:
Hands-on collection for the DoctorAssistant bot (CLAUDE.md 3.9 / 3.10).

Folder A is the **Responses API** — what both bots actually use.
Folder B is **Chat Completions** — the alternative, shown doing the same job so the difference is visible rather than described.

## Setup

1. Open the collection's **Variables** tab.
2. Paste your key into `openai_api_key` (CURRENT VALUE column only — that column is not exported, so the key never leaves your machine).
3. Run requests top to bottom within a folder. Later requests reuse ids captured by earlier ones.

## What to watch

- `usage.input_tokens` on every response. That is the number `bot_token_usage` records.
- In **A2**, the request body carries only the new message — but `usage.input_tokens` still bills for the whole conversation. `previous_response_id` saves upload, not tokens.
- In **B2**, the request body carries the entire transcript. Same tokens, much bigger upload, and the transcript is yours to store.
- In **A4 vs B4**, compare what you have to hand-assemble to return a tool result.

item.name: A · Responses API (what the bot uses)
item.description: The API both DoctorAssistant versions call. Stateful: OpenAI keeps the conversation when `store` is true, and you refer back to it with `previous_response_id`.

request.description:
Maps to `OpenAiToolCallingBrain.respond()`'s first call, minus the tools.

`instructions` is the system prompt. `input` is the user's message. `store: true` is what makes the response id reusable in A2.

The test script saves `id` into `previous_response_id` for you.

exec: '(note: higher than A1, even though you sent less)');

body.raw:
{
  "model": "{{model}}",
  "instructions": "You are the appointment assistant for Willow Lane Clinic. Be warm and brief. Plain text only, no markdown.",
  "previous_response_id": "{{previous_response_id}}",
  "input": "what did I just say to you?",
  "store": true
}

request.description:
**The lesson request.** The body contains no history at all — just a pointer and the new message. The model still answers correctly, because OpenAI holds the transcript.

Now look at `usage.input_tokens`: **higher than A1**. You uploaded less and were billed more. That is the whole truth about `previous_response_id` — it saves bandwidth and bookkeeping, never tokens.

This is `bot_conversation_state.last_response_id` in action.

**Also try:** delete `instructions` from this body and re-send. The model forgets the plain-text rule, because instructions apply to ONE call and are not carried by the chain. That is the exact bug that made `OpenAiToolCallingBrain` re-send them every round.

exec: console.log('no function call this time — try a more specific question');

request.description:
This is `ClinicTool.asFunctionTool()` written out by hand — the exact JSON your enum builds.

The response's `output` array will contain a `function_call` item, not a message:

```json
{ "type": "function_call", "call_id": "fc_...",
  "name": "get_available_slots",
  "arguments": "{\"date\":\"2026-09-03\",\"specialty\":\"Cardiology\"}" }
```

**`arguments` is a string.** The model wrote text; nothing executed. That is the whole point.

Note `strict: true` requires EVERY property listed in `required` — which is why an optional argument is typed `["string", "null"]` rather than left out.

The test script captures `call_id` for A4.

item.name: A4 · With tools — round 2 (you send the result back)

exec: console.log(more ? 'model wants ANOTHER tool → this is round 3' : 'model replied → loop ends here');

request.description:
You are playing the part of `ClinicToolExecutor` — the JSON in `output` is what your SQL would have returned.

Four things worth noticing:

1. **`call_id` must match** what round 1 sent. Get it wrong and the API rejects the whole request.
2. **`output` is a string**, not an object — a JSON document inside a JSON string.
3. **`tools` is sent again.** The model needs the menu on every round.
4. **`instructions` is sent again.** Drop it and watch the reply change format — this is the bug from `OpenAiToolCallingBrain`'s comment at line 182.

The response should now be plain text with no `function_call` — that is `calls.isEmpty()` becoming true and the `while` loop returning.

**Version 1 in miniature.** Everything the model could need is jammed into `instructions` — doctors, hours, bookings, and the two separately-headed lists from the cross-patient leak fix.

The reply comes back as JSON matching `BotDecision`. `action: "BOOK"` is the model *requesting* a write; Java then re-validates and either books or throws the model's text away.

This is what the Java SDK generates for you from the record via `builder.text(BotDecision.class)`.

**Try this:** paste your real 15,000-character prompt from `bot_prompt_log.system_prompt` in here and compare `usage.input_tokens` against A3.

body.raw:
{
  "model": "{{model}}",
  "instructions": "You are the appointment assistant for Willow Lane Clinic.",
  "input": "tell me in three sentences what you can help with",
  "stream": true,
  "store": true
}

request.description:
One extra field — `"stream": true` — and the response becomes `text/event-stream`.

Postman shows the raw SSE frames. Look for:

- `response.created` — first, carries the id
- `response.output_text.delta` — dozens of these, each a few characters. **These are the `bot_stream_delta` frames in your DevTools screenshot.**
- `response.completed` — last, carries the ENTIRE finished response including `usage`

That last one is why `send()` can return a plain `Response` while streaming: the completed event hands over everything the blocking call would have.

Fetch a response by id. Proof that `store: true` really does keep it server-side.

**Try this:** paste an OLD `last_response_id` from your `bot_conversation_state` table. If it 404s with `param: previous_response_id`, you have just reproduced `ExpiredConversationException` by hand — the sawtooth drops in the cost chart are exactly this.

Note what you CANNOT do here: query it, search it, or aggregate over it. That is why long-term memory ("remembers your dizziness from last week") needs your own table, not this.

Removes it from OpenAI's side. Run A7 afterwards to see the 404.

Useful for deliberately breaking a chain and watching your app's recovery path fire.

item.name: B · Chat Completions API (the alternative)
item.description:
The same jobs, done the portable way. Stateless: there is no `previous_response_id`, so YOU carry the transcript in `messages` on every single request.

This is what Spring AI targets, and what you would be writing if the bot had to run against Azure, Bedrock or a local model.

request.description:
Compare with A1.

- `instructions` → a `system` **message inside the array**
- `input` → a `user` message
- no `store`, because nothing is stored

The reply lives at `choices[0].message.content`, and usage at `usage.prompt_tokens` (not `input_tokens` — different field names for the same thing).

item.name: B2 · Multi-turn — you carry the transcript

request.description:
**The direct comparison to A2.** Same question, same answer — but look at the body.

Everything the conversation has ever contained is here, and you sent all of it. In A2 you sent one id and one sentence.

`usage.prompt_tokens` will be close to A2's `input_tokens`, because **the billing is the same**. What differs is:

- the upload size
- who stores the transcript (you)
- what happens when it outgrows the context window (your problem — see windowing)

At turn 60 of your conversation `3:8`, this array would hold 120 messages.

**Note the system message is `messages[0]`.** If Version 1 ran on this API, its 15,000-character clinic snapshot would sit here — and you would have to rewrite index 0 every turn or accumulate contradictory copies of what is booked.

exec: console.log('copy the assistant message verbatim into B4');

request.description:
Same tool, **different envelope**. Compare the shape with A3:

| | Responses (A3) | Chat Completions (B3) |
|---|---|---|
| tool shape | `{type, name, description, parameters}` flat | `{type, function: {name, ...}}` nested |
| where the call lands | `output[]` as `function_call` | `choices[0].message.tool_calls[]` |
| the id field | `call_id` | `id` |

A port between the two is not a config change. This is exactly the rewrite cost CLAUDE.md §5 names for a provider swap.

item.name: B4 · With tools — round 2 (assistant + tool messages)

request.description:
**Replace both `PASTE_tool_call_id_FROM_B3` placeholders** with the id the B3 console logged.

This is the request that shows the real cost of not having `previous_response_id`. Compare it to A4:

- A4 sent: a pointer, ONE `function_call_output`, the tools.
- B4 sends: the system message, the user message, **the assistant's own tool-call message echoed back verbatim**, the `tool` message, and the tools.

And the pairing rules are strict:

1. Every `tool_calls` entry needs a matching `role: "tool"` message.
2. They pair by `tool_call_id` — `id` on the assistant side, `tool_call_id` on the tool side.
3. Order matters: assistant message first, then its tool results.

Break any of the three and the API 400s. **That bookkeeping is what `previous_response_id` does for you** — not the tokens.

Same idea as A6, different frames. Chat Completions streams `choices[0].delta.content` chunks and finishes with `data: [DONE]`.

**Note `stream_options.include_usage`.** Without it, a streamed Chat Completions response gives you NO token counts at all. The Responses API's `response.completed` event carries `usage` unconditionally — which is why `OpenAiToolCallingBrain` can stream and still fill in `bot_token_usage` without asking for anything extra.
